summary: Columbia County site: a 1934 field report calls it the old Enterprise lookout, says the road was opened, and says no tower was built there.

events.note: Field report calls it the old Enterprise lookout; the old road was opened; no tower built there, and a tower had been built on Clatskanie Heights (Benson)

evidence.supports: Site is listed under Columbia County
evidence.quote: COLUMBIA COUNTY Baker Point Benson Mountain Clatskanie Mountain Enterprise Point Mansfield Mountain

evidence.supports: Agency is the Oregon Department of Forestry
1934 field report: old lookout about a quarter mile off the road, old road opened
evidence.quote: The old Enterprise lookout is off the road about 1/4 mile but they opened up the old road to the lookout.

evidence.supports: No tower built at the site; a tower had been built on Clatskanie Heights (Benson)
evidence.quote: They did not build a tower there and I do not think it is necessary, as they have built a tower on Clatskanie Heights (Benson).

evidence.supports: The 1934 field report is by P.S. King

sources.title: Enterprise Point - Forest Lookouts (Columbia County entry, quoting P.S. King Field Report, 1934)

notes_for_editor: One source only, and it is a secondhand transcription of a 1934 field report. Enterprise Point does not appear in the firelookout.org Oregon county list, so there is no NHLR or FFLOS record to check status against. The 1934 'tower on Clatskanie Heights (Benson)' is not identified with a registry entry; the registry lists Benson Mountain and Clatskanie Mountain towers as Gone, and a demonstrationforest.org search snippet (not read) says the Clatskanie Mountain tower was moved to Hopkins Demonstration Forest. Check that conflict before writing a Clatskanie story. The story says the report gives 'Benson' as the name of the Clatskanie Heights tower; the source shows it only in parentheses, so whether King himself used the name is not established.
